title: AS2 compiler: 'key in obj' uses hasOwnProperty (misses prototype chain)
description:
The 'in' binary operator (key in obj) is implemented in packages/core/src/as2/compiler.ts (~line 1773) by emitting ActionCallMethod (0x52) to call obj.hasOwnProperty(key). This is semantically wrong: in AS2/ECMAScript, 'key in obj' should check the full prototype chain, not just own properties. For example, '"toString" in {}' should return true (inherited from Object.prototype) but the current implementation returns false.

There is no ActionIn opcode in AVM1 (0x60 is ActionBitAnd). Task 0085 noted '(6) in operator — ActionEnumerate + linear search (approximation)' but the implemented approach uses hasOwnProperty which behaves differently. A correct approximation would need to walk the prototype chain using __proto__ or check via 'prop' in obj using ActionGetMember approach.

Fix approach: emit a GetMember probe — push obj, push key, ActionGetMember; then check if the result is undefined (note: distinguishing 'not present' from 'present but undefined' is hard in AVM1 without ActionIn; the hasOwnProperty approach may be acceptable for own-property cases if documented, but any code relying on inherited property detection will be wrong). Alternatively, document as a known limitation if the fix is too invasive.

Location: packages/core/src/as2/compiler.ts, compileBinaryExpr(), the 'in' branch at ~line 1773.
